newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea offers lesson in exam security.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea offers lesson in exam security.

text.p: No one can say South Korea doesn't take its school examinations seriously.

A group of professors and teachers responsible for devising questions for the recent college entrance tests were released on Wednesday after being confined in a Seoul hotel for a month, the Korea Times reported on Thursday.
Sixty-nine college professors and 46 high school teachers moved into the hotel on October 14.
To prevent possible leaks, the hotel was sealed off. The windows of the first floor were papered over and barbed-wire fencing was erected around the building.
Armed police kept a tight watch over the hotel and all telephone lines were cut, except for a special hot-line.
Of nearly 820,000 students registered for the state-run exams, 795,403 took the tests on Wednesday.

The entire nation froze to make way for students rushing to testing centres. Government offices, banks and financial markets delayed opening for 30 minutes to ease rush-hour congestion. Private citizens were asked to report for work an hour late.
